title: Scope
instructions: Scope is about WHERE a variable exists and can be used.
A variable made inside a function is local — it only exists inside that function. Outside, it's as if it never existed.
A variable made outside all functions is global — every function can see and use it.
Local variables keep functions tidy and independent. Reach for globals sparingly.
Here, global is shared, but a variable made inside a function would not be visible in main.
task: Print the global variable from inside main so the output ends with:  global = 100
hint:
global is visible everywhere, so just print it:

    printf("global = %d\n", global);
